correctness.rationale: The uniform random edge priorities coincide with rate-1/N independent exponential edge clocks. Directly counting eligible AB and BB edges yields the exact density-dependent chain with transitions (-1,-1) at AB/N and (0,-2) at B(B-1)/(2N), and limiting drift (-ab,-ab-b^2). The strictly positive first integral h(a,b)=a exp(-b/a) is conserved: its gradient (e^(-b/a)(1+b/a),-e^(-b/a)) has zero dot product with this drift; the fluid b tends to zero while a tends to r=alpha exp(-(1-alpha)/alpha). For fixed sufficiently late T, a(T)-b(T)>r/2; uniform fluid approximation gives A(T)-B(T)>rN/3 with high probability. Since A-B is nondecreasing at every deposition, cross-edges remain available whenever B>0, B is exhausted, and tau-T=O_p(log N) by comparison with a pure-death chain of rates >=(r/3)B. Thus terminal U=A(tau) with high probability, giving the law of large numbers and bounded expectation convergence. Taylor expansion on a>=r/3 gives the h-generator O(1/N), which integrated to tau gives o_p(N^-1/2). The martingale differences for AB and BB jumps are -e^(-b/a)(b/a)/N and +2e^(-b/a)/N, respectively. The scaled quadratic-variation density is Q=e^(-2b/a)(b^3/a+2b^2); each scaled jump is O(N^-1/2), giving Lindeberg. For t>=T, bracket density is <=C b; conditional expected integral of b is bounded by 3b(T)/r, so the martingale tail vanishes uniformly in the required sequential limits. The finite-horizon martingale CLT extends to the terminal state. With u=log(a/r), b=a u, du/dt=-b, integrating Q gives v=r integral_0^L e^(-u)(u^2+2u)du=r[4-(L+2)^2 exp(-L)]>0. Independently checked five finite complete-edge-order distributions, including 362880 orders for A=2,B=3, and a separate recursive count-chain law; checked finite exact/float moments at three N values and three alphas and symbolic h and bracket identities. These tests verify modeling and algebra only, not the general CLT.
residual_risks: The terminal martingale CLT relies on conventional density-dependent fluid and martingale limit theorems plus a localized tail argument, not a formal machine-check.
Finite tests do not establish the all-N theorem; proof applies only to fixed alpha strictly in (0,1), not endpoint-uniform, Berry–Esseen or large deviations.

value.rationale: The complete split graph is a canonical deterministic dense inhomogeneous graph with a natural clique-plus-independent decomposition, not an arbitrary parameter slice. Greedy edge-dimer deposition on this graph is a natural irreversible kinetic process with a surprising positive jammed unmatched density despite the existence of perfect matchings. The explicit Gaussian fluctuation law and strictly positive computable variance capture the finite-size uncertainty of the entire matching, not just a mean or a standard special-function identity. Reaching a terminal stochastic state from a finite-time density-dependent CLT requires the substantive late-time separation, martingale drift and bracket-tail analysis supplied in the proof. This quantitative natural invariant is mathematically valuable even without Berry–Esseen or endpoint-uniform extensions.
residual_risks: No finite-size Berry–Esseen bound, near-alpha-endpoint regime or large deviations proven.
Practical performance implications are interpretive rather than a theorem for all greedy matchers.

limitations: Fixed interior alpha only, no uniform endpoints or error rates.
